Drakensberg Choir Boys

By: Liz Fish | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Two boys, from two very different backgrounds, one amazing school where they get to spend their lives singing

Unique Selling Point:
This is story about two boys from different walks of life, from different parts of the country and a remarkable school. 10 years old Ethan Palangwe of Mitchells Plain is living his dream, he has just been selected for a solo part in the Drakensberg Boys choir latest release ”Butter” a major achievement as it’s only his 2nd year at Drakensberg Boys Choir school. He is excelling academically, in sports and passing his music theory with flying colours having never had any musical training before auditioning. He is a wise compassionate child.

Summary:
Ethan’s home is in Mitchells Plain, his mom is a teacher aid and his dad works for the City of Cape Town Law enforcement and he is one of 4 siblings. He went to Mandalay Primary in Mitchells Plain and was destined to survive the streets on Eastridge, dodging gangs and bullets. His mom Candice loves music and singing and noticed her 8 year olds talent. She spotted an advert in the Mitchells Plain community newspaper that the Drakensberg boys choir was doing auditions at SACS in Rondebosch she took “Pumkin” along. He was one of 30 boys selected from 1600 to join the prestigious Drakensberg School choir.
10-year-old Michelle Dittberner grew up in Hillcrest in KZN to relatively well-off middleclass parents and never really showed any particular musical talent as far as his mother was concerned. As a 9 year old he was being bullied by the other kids at school. Megan his mother needed to find a new school for her child and while on holiday in the Drakensberg they visited the school to buy a new CD. A casual chat with a teacher turned into an offer for an audition which Megan tried to dissuade them from doing and to her surprise Michele was accepted.
Ethan and Michael have become extremely close and Megan and Mark Dittberner have “adopted” Ethan hosting him on weekends and short holidays and have become very close and supportive to his parents Candice and Kagiso. Little Ethan comforted Mark when he dropped Micheal off at school saying ” The 3 weeks you cannot see your son is harder for the parents than the boys, I will look after him. We are like brothers here” Quite exceptional for a 10 year old to approach an emotional adult he had never met before.


Further information:
The Drakensberg Boys school choir is a remarkable school nestle in the foothills of the Drakensberg established in 1967. It has 79 boys from all walks of life across South Africa. Dave Cato the head master aim is to be far more than a school but a launchpad for these talented children, integrating their cultures through music and movement and providing them with an exceptional academic base. The boys are only allowed one pair of civvies so there is no distinction between their different backgrounds. Many children are from poor rural communities but when the boys enter the school the idea is they build them equally. It’s a haven for boys to grow safely and grow their talent free from the bulling and crime that dominates so many young boys lives.
They do an annual international tour but COVID has stopped that and the school is struggling financially as a result. Drakensberg Boys Choir school has produced many exceptional music talents- The Bala Brothers being one of many. The boys are between 9 and 15 and when they get to Grade 8 the top schools in the area, Hilton, Kearsney start scouting and auditioning the boys to get scholarships to complete their education in these private schools. Many don’t pursue a career in music but the grounding they received there sets them up for life- Wayde Williams grew up in Bonteheuwel on the Cape Flats and is now the BMW and Jaguar representative is a “Drakie” graduate and his supporting the Palangwe family.
It's a feel good story and an opportunity to tell the story of an exceptional school through the eyes of young Ethan and Michael and their parents who are supporting each other in a country full of trauma and poor education and boys beaten down by this environment.

LINK Drakensberg boys choir, it’s a South African institution- world renowned for it’s exceptional coral performances,but who are the individuals that make up this elite group of boys. I am about to meet two Drakies boys that have found a home at the school and in one another

Script: It’s a huge day for 12 year old Ethan Palaganwe, it’s the Founders concert and his 1st solo
Ethans solo
Claire Do you guys get nervous before concerts?
Ethan: For me as a soloist, I'm really nervous. My heart starts pounding when I go up front and when I sing. But when there's another person with me, it's way easier.
Ethan solo and hugg

Parents standing around outside the concert

Ethan: I got this voice of mine from my mom because she's a top class singer
Upsound of Candice singing at home
Script: Candice and Kagisho Palangwe live in Eastridge in Mitchells Plain, Ethan who’s called pumpkin by is dad, is the eldest of 4 children
Candice: Oh. It all started when I saw this ad in the in the newspaper, and Ethan’s loves singing,.., he looked up to me and that is where he developed his love for music.
Claire: What do you love best about being a Drakie ?
Ethan: So I love that the school gets us to tour to different countries and continents. We support all the people that travel around, and so many people are just there for each other
BREAK of dawn sounds and the drone sunrise
Ethan thats one thing that I like about the school. Waking up every morning and looking up to the mountain.
SCRIPT: The safety and the freedom to roam, has really changed their lives
Kagiso: every parent would want to stay in a community whereby there's a park, your child is safe. You don't, you'll get boys standing on the corner doing or selling illegal substances. ….even when he comes home, he is at Pollsmoor, the big gate school is locked. You never sees outside, you're not even allowed to go to shop stuff like that or else would go with him to the shop. We feel we don't want him to become part of the statistics in our country.
Pause with boys playing soccer-
Link: Micheal came here quite by chance, his family had brought him on holiday to escape a particularly difficult time in his schooling
Micheal: at my old school, they'd take my bag, throw it onto the grass that I was not allowed on to and they would force me to go on it, and then I'd get punished. And they'd kick me on my shins, and they'd throw me around. I'd go to the bathroom and act sick and fake vomit so I can go to the nurse and go home because I just didn't want to be around.
Script: The bullying became so extreme, Michael’s life was a living hell. His mother Megan Dittberner brought the family away on holiday. A chance visit to the school to buy a Drakensberg boys choir CD - changed their worlds
Megan “Michael was speaking about his favourite songs on the CD and the choir director came out and said why have you not auditioned and I was in the background going, They've borders, he is 10 I'm not ready to send my child off into the world…... Anyway, he went and he came back and he said, wonderful ear for music and they'd love to have him.
Script: Headmaster Dave Cato says this is often the case
Clair: the perception is that you have to be exceptional to be accepted here.
Dave: That's not true at all….. The vast majority of boys have no musical training before getting here if a boy has a reasonable ear and can hold a tune. Our staff are trained to turn that boy into a fine chorister.
Script: It’s a very small school with just 73 boys currently and Cato knows them all
Upsound wishing happy birthday and singing happy birthday
Script: When the boys enroll they go through an intense training program, neither Ethan or Michael had any prior musical training
They had to earn the right to sing in the choir, which means perfecting 21 songs, and then- singing a solo for the Grade 9’s and the teachers.
Upsound
Only then could they undergo the 55 year old ritual of being awarded the blue and jabbo, the iconic waistcoat and white ruff

Ethan: Well, we love singing. So I wouldn't really say that it's hard because, um, singing is our talent at first.
Michael: At 1st For me, it was a bit difficult standing for 2 hours everyday in. In the auditorium or sitting down doing my tests as a new boy. Um, but now I'm used to it, so now it's not a big deal for me.

Script: It’s a friendship that's grown beyond the boys, Megan makes sure to share those special performances with his parents
Kagiso: The first time we saw him, we both like cried
Candice: The entire concert through.

Kagiso: COVID has really caused a lot of challenges and it has crippled big businesses, huge organizations and those sort of people that used to contribute towards Ethan tuition fees

Candice “I've been performing with my band, and I got the opportunity to work on the MEC cruise ship. So I get to provide for the family as well.
